evidence.note: Agent enters plan mode and writes a plan.md, indicating some upfront intent to structure the work, but the plan is a feature list rather than ordered, independently-verifiable milestones with done-checks.

Writes the entire decoder — common.h, bitstream, fse, huffman, sequence, block, frame/zstd_decompress — in a bottom-up dependency order, but never compiles or verifies any single component in isolation. Loose implicit ordering, no per-component completion criteria.
The first 'make && ../test.sh' occurs only after the whole decoder is already written — the defining signature of a monolithic push with no staged verification.

All debugging is reactive whole-system iteration against test.sh (audio.wav, img.bmp failing); no localized milestone verification, so bugs in Huffman/FSE/bitstream are hard to isolate — exactly the tangle the dimension warns about.

reasoning: The agent wrote every component of the decoder before running or testing anything (first compile at step 47), which is the behavior anchor 0 describes. It is lifted slightly above pure 0 by a loose implicit dependency ordering (bitstream→FSE→Huffman→sequence→block→frame) and a drafted plan.md, but there were no explicit milestones, no per-component done-checks, and no incremental verification, so failures stayed unlocalized.
